{{short description|Datasets on COVID-19}}
'''COVID-19 datasets''' are public databases for sharing case data and medical information related to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].

== Aggregate statistics ==

=== Global ===
* [[Johns Hopkins University|Johns Hopkins]] Coronavirus Resource Center: Global aggregated data including cases, testing, contact tracing, and vaccine development<ref>{{Cite web|title=Home|url=https://coronavirus.jhu.edu/|access-date=2020-09-18|website=Johns Hopkins Coronavirus Resource Center|language=en}}</ref>
* [[World Health Organization]] (WHO) Coronavirus Disease Dashboard: a database of confirmed cases and deaths reported globally and broken down by region.<ref>{{Cite web|title=WHO Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19) Dashboard|url=https://covid19.who.int/|access-date=2020-09-18|website=covid19.who.int|language=en}}</ref> This database is part of the WHO Health Data Platform.<ref>{{Cite web|title=World Health Data Platform - WHO|url=https://www.who.int/data|access-date=2020-09-18|website=www.who.int|language=en}}</ref>
* COVID-19 Africa Open Data Project: a volunteer-run database and dashboard reporting region, country and district level case counts, deaths, healthcare worker infections, healthcare services and urgent needs.<ref>{{cite web |title=COVID-19 Africa Open Data |url=http://covid-19-africa.sen.ovh/ |access-date=16 November 2020}}</ref>

== Data hubs ==
* [https://hdruk.ac.uk Health Data Research UK] provides a searchable registry of health data resources from the United Kingdom, including [https://web.www.healthdatagateway.org/search?search=COVID-19&tab=Datasets COVID-19 related datasets].
* NIH Open Access Datasets: The [[National Institutes of Health]] provide open-access data and computational resources related to COVID-19.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Open-Access Data and Computational Resources to Address COVID-19 {{!}} Data Science at NIH|url=https://datascience.nih.gov/covid-19-open-access-resources|access-date=2020-10-13|website=datascience.nih.gov}}</ref>
* COVID-19 Open Research Dataset (CORD-19): The [[Semantic Scholar]] project of the [[Allen Institute for AI]] hosts CORD-19, a public dataset of academic articles about COVID-19 and related research.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CORD-19 |url=https://www.semanticscholar.org/cord19|access-date=2020-10-13|website=Semantic Scholar}}</ref> The dataset is updated daily and includes both peer-reviewed articles and preprints.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Analysis of COVID-19 publications identifies research gaps|url=https://eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2020-09/cp-aoc091720.php|access-date=2020-10-13|website=EurekAlert!|language=en|archive-date=2021-01-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210101000851/https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2020-09/cp-aoc091720.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> CORD-19 was originally released on March 16, 2020, by researchers and leaders from the Allen Institute for AI, [[Chan Zuckerberg Initiative]], [[Center for Security and Emerging Technology|Georgetown University's Center for Security and Emerging Technhology]], [[Microsoft]], and the [[United States National Library of Medicine|National Library of Medicine]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Call to Action to the Tech Community on New Machine Readable COVID-19 Dataset|url=https://trumpwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefings-statements/call-action-tech-community-new-machine-readable-covid-19-dataset/|access-date=2020-10-13|via=[[NARA|National Archives]]|work=[[whitehouse.gov]]|language=en-US}}</ref> The dataset is created through the use of [[text mining]] of the current research literature.<ref>{{Cite web|title=NLM Leverages Data, Text Mining to Sharpen COVID-19 Research Databases|url=https://governmentciomedia.com/nlm-leverages-data-text-mining-sharpen-covid-19-research-databases|access-date=2020-10-13|website=governmentciomedia.com|date=11 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

== Topic-specific and special-interest resources ==

=== Genomics ===
* Consensus genome data for [[SARS-CoV-2]] is available through [[GISAID]] for registered users<ref>{{cite web|title=GISAID|url=https://www.gisaid.org/|access-date=29 December 2020|website=www.gisaid.org}}</ref> and included in an interactive [[Phylogenetic tree]] dashboard <ref name="Nexstrain SARS-CoV-2">{{cite web|title=Nexstrain SARS-CoV-2 Dashboard|url=https://nextstrain.org/ncov/global|access-date=29 December 2020|website=nextstrain.org}}</ref> on [[Nextstrain]], an open-source pathogen [[genome]] data project.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nextstrain|url=https://docs.nextstrain.org/en/latest/learn/about-nextstrain.html|access-date=29 December 2020|website=docs.nextstrain.org}}</ref>

=== Imaging (Radiology) ===
* Characteristic imaging features on chest [[radiographs]] and [[computed tomography]] (CT) of people who are symptomatic include asymmetric peripheral [[Ground-glass opacity|ground-glass opacities]] without [[pleural effusion]]s.<ref name="AJR">{{cite journal |vauthors=Li Y, Xia L |title=Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19): Role of Chest CT in Diagnosis and Management |journal=American Journal of Roentgenology |pages=1280–1286 |date=March 2020|volume=214 |issue=6 |pmid=32130038 |doi=10.2214/AJR.20.22954|s2cid=212416282 |doi-access=free }}</ref> The [[University of Montreal]] and [[Mila (research institute)|Mila]] created the "COVID-19 Image Data Collection" in March which is a public data repository of chest imaging.<ref name="mila-covid">{{cite web |title=COVID-19 related projects |at=COVID-19 image data collection |website=Mila |access-date=12 July 2020 | url=https://mila.quebec/en/covid-19/}}</ref><ref name="covid-image-github">{{cite web |title=COVID-19 image data collection |url=https://github.com/ieee8023/covid-chestxray-dataset |website=GitHub |access-date=12 July 2020}}</ref><ref name="covid-image-arxiv">{{cite arXiv |last1=Cohen |first1=Joseph |title=COVID-19 image data collection |eprint=2003.11597 |date=25 March 2020|class=eess.IV }}</ref> The Medical Imaging Databank in Valencian Region released a large dataset of chest imaging from Spain.<ref name="BIMCV-COVID19">{{cite web |title=BIMCV-COVID19, Datasets related to COVID19's pathology course |url=https://bimcv.cipf.es/bimcv-projects/bimcv-covid19/ |website=Medical Imaging Databank in Valencian Region Medical |access-date=12 July 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=de la Iglesia Vayá |first1=Maria |title=BIMCV COVID-19+: a large annotated dataset of RX and CT images from COVID-19 patients |date=1 June 2020 |class=eess.IV |eprint=2006.01174 }}</ref> The [[Italian Society of Medical and Interventional Radiology|Italian Radiological Society]] is compiling an international online database of imaging findings for confirmed cases.<ref name="Cx70C">{{cite web |title=COVID-19 Database |url= https://www.sirm.org/category/senza-categoria/covid-19/ | website=Società Italiana di Radiologia Medica e Interventistica |access-date=2020-03-11|language=it}}</ref> Online radiology case sharing platforms such as [[European Society of Radiology#Eurorad|Eurorad]] and [[Radiopaedia]] serve as platforms for sharing COVID-19 case data and imaging.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pneumothorax and pneumomediastinum: a rare complication in the evolution of COVID-19 pneumonia. |url=https://www.eurorad.org/case/16844 |website=Eurorad |access-date=12 July 2020}}</ref><ref name="radiopaedia-covid">{{cite web |last1=Bell |first1=Daniel |last2=Knipe |first2=Henry |title=COVID-19 (summary) |url=https://radiopaedia.org/articles/covid-19-summary |website=Radiopaedia |access-date=12 July 2020}}</ref>
